commit.message:
Extractor option to return keypoints in corner convention (#191)

LightGlue so far assumes keypoints are in the center-coordinate system,
i.e. (0, 0) is the center of the top-left pixel (OpenCV convention).
Most systems use corner convention (0.5, 0.5 for center of top-left
pixel), which is mathematically nicer. It is the default of COLMAP, too.

In this PR we add an option to all extractors to output keypoints in
"corner" coordinate system. For now this is optional, but in the near
future we will make this the default for ALL extractors.

LightGlue matcher is unchanged, and still assumes coordinates in
"center" coordinate system.

Also fixes some small bugs in SIFT (related to this coordinate system
mismatch).

+        # Patch origin --> default to center of pixel

+        if self.conf.origin not in ("center", "corner"):

+
+    @property
+    def coords_offset(self) -> float:
+        """Offset added to pixel-center keypoints to output them in self.conf.origin."""
+        return 0.5 if self.conf.origin == "corner" else 0.0
+
+    def scale_keypoints(
+        self, keypoints: torch.Tensor, scales: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Scale keypoints by a scale factor"""
+        if self.conf.origin == "corner":
+            return keypoints / scales[None]  # origin at corner of pixel
+        return (keypoints + 0.5) / scales[None] - 0.5  # origin at center of pixel
